newsitem.title: USA: IRS defers business electronic tax payment penalties.
newsitem.headline: IRS defers business electronic tax payment penalties.

text.p: The Internal Revenue Service said Monday it deferred for six months imposing penalties on small businesses that did not make tax payments electronically, as required by law.

The penalty of 10 percent on tax deposits will not be imposed through Dec. 31 to allow businesses an additional six months to comply with the requirement of paying taxes electronically by telephone or computer, the IRS said.

Businesses that deposited more than $50,000 in federal payroll taxes such as withholding and Social Security in 1995 were required to enroll in the Electronic Federal Tax Payment System and pay taxes electronically by July 1, the IRS said.
"I'm pleased the IRS has agreed to delay any penalties for not complying with this mandate," said Assistant Senate Majority Leader Don Nickles, an Oklahoma Republican.
Nickles has introduced legislation that would put the threshold for required electronic filing at $5 million annual payroll tax deposits and make it voluntary for smaller businesses to participate.

Nickles said hundreds of thousands of business owners were still not aware of the requirement or the penalties and that many business owners who enrolled in the tax payment system found their banks charged a fee for electronic transactions or did not offer the service.

"We have announced this penalty relief to encourage businesses to use and get comfortable with the system," Michael Dolan, IRS acting commissioner, said in a letter to Nickles. "If businesses encounter any problems they will have time to get help and make adjustments, rather than face a penalty," he wrote.

A provision in the North American Free Trade Agreement directed the IRS to begin collecting by electronic funds transfer a gradually increasing percentage of total depository taxes such as Social Security, income tax withheld, corporate income and estimated taxes, and various excise taxes.
About 1,500 larger businesses that deposited more than $47 million in payroll taxes in 1993 or 1994 were required to begin depositing their taxes electronically last year.
The requirement for small businesses was initially set for Jan. 1, but was delayed until July 1 through a provision in the Small Business Job Protection Act.
The IRS said of the almost 1.2 million businesses required to begin using the electronic payment system by July 1, more than 1.1 million have enrolled.
